topic: Benjamin Franklin calming waves with oil
script: Oil film snaps a windy pond silent in London. 1773. Clapham Common pond. Benjamin Franklin holds a small vial. Royal Society gentlemen watch from the bank, doubtful. Gusts roughen the whole surface. How? Franklin uncorks the vial and tips a teaspoon. The oil touches the pond and races outward. A glassy patch grows beside the choppy water. It spreads several yards across the pond. Sailors even carry oil to pour near surf. The gentlemen scoff and call it sailor talk. Here, the calm edge draws a clear line. The oil film cuts the surface pull, or tension. The smallest ripples fail, so bigger chop cannot build. It’s like a drop of soap stilling sink ripples. Franklin writes the Royal Society with what he saw. He credits a sea captain and Cavallo for urging tests. The pond goes quiet where the film has spread. A tiny film outmuscles wind on water. A teaspoon of oil snaps a windy pond silent.
